lead_text:
I've started the `hw/` design record for the latch lever. Everything the brief states is in it, and the record validator passes with no findings. Work now stops at GROUND, because the flow needs your answers before it can compare routes at INTENT. The concept stage (L0), the variant gate and the layout stage (L1) haven't started, so no concepts or models exist yet. Setup found FreeCAD 1.1.4 and all the CAD tools; their warm-up is running in the background.

**What's recorded**
- **10 requirements (REQ-001…010), one per point in your brief:**
  - two M4 screws to the panel
  - Ø6 × 30 steel pin with DIN 6799-5 ring grooves
  - lever about 80 mm long, 8 mm thick at the hub
  - 0–75° travel with hard stops at both ends
  - 0.3 mm axial gap at each cheek
  - reamed clearance fit on the pin
  - at least 1 mm clearance to the bracket in all poses, laid out at 1.1 mm (the flow's default 0.1 mm margin)
  - 30 N at the handle
  - PETG printed on your MK4
  - quantity 4

  Each has a planned verification row.
- **Use case, partly filled in:** purpose, indoor use, 0–75° range, quantity 4, and two 30 N handle loads (one opening, one closing). Everything else stays unknown and is linked to a question.
- **MK4 printer profile:** build volume and 0.4 mm nozzle, as you stated them. It has no calibration, so it claims no achievable accuracy.
- **Direction convention:** pivot along Y; X along the bracket toward the handle when latched; Z pointing out of the panel.

**Questions before I continue.** For each one I've suggested an answer you can accept as is:

| # | Question | Suggested answer |
|---|---|---|
| Q-001 | Are the 4 units prototypes or end-use parts? | Working prototype, used for real indoors |
| Q-002 | What does the latch hold, and does the lever hook onto a catch, or just rest on the 0° stop? | Rests on the 0° stop; no catch on the panel |
| Q-003/004 | Temperature range, heat, humidity, chemicals? | 10–35 °C, dry room; zinc-plated or stainless pin |
| Q-005 | Which way does the 30 N push go? Does the lever get slammed onto the stops? | Either way, including pushing against both stops; no slamming |
| Q-006 | How often is it used, how long must it last, and should it swing freely or hold by friction? | About 10 times a day, 10,000 cycles total; swings freely |
| Q-008 | What happens if it breaks? Any standards or other approver? | Inconvenience only; no standards; you approve |
| Q-009 | Budget and lead time? | Not limited |
| Q-010 | Who prints and reams, with which reamer? Can anything be outsourced? | You do it, with a Ø6 H7 hand reamer; pin and rings bought, nothing else outsourced |
| Q-011 | What may the release claim, and is a physical test needed? | CAD plus analysis only; no physical test claim |
| Q-012 | M4 screw type and fitting order? | DIN 912 M4 socket-head screws; fit the screws before the lever |
| Q-013 | General tolerance for the drawings? | ISO 2768-m |
| Q-014 | Which PETG brand, and which print settings? | Prusament PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 4 perimeters, 40 % gyroid infill |
| Q-015 | Panel material and thickness, how the screws hold, any hole spacing or footprint limit? | Panel and spacing open; through-bolts with nuts |
| Q-016 | Should generated files (STEP, GLB, renders, check results) go into git (using Git LFS for STEP/GLB)? | No, keep them out of git |

Reply with answers or corrections, or "accept the suggestions". After that I'll record the INTENT comparison of manufacturing options and ask you to approve it. Then come the specification, 2–3 concept variants for you to choose from, and the layout build with its checks and LAYOUT freeze gate. Nothing will be approved or frozen without your explicit OK.

reply:
Answers from the user:
- Working prototype representative of intended use: four latches on our own cabinet.
- It holds a hinged cabinet door shut against a keeper on the frame. When latched, the door can pull on the lever with up to 10 N; the 30 N hand load is the larger case.
- Indoor workshop, 10 to 35 °C, dry.
- Up to 30 N by hand at the lever's handle end, about 80 mm from the pivot, in either direction of travel, including against each stop. No impact or vibration rating.
- The lever turns about the pin from 0° latched to 75° open, with hard stops on the bracket at both ends. About 20 cycles a day; no life target is claimed.
- Low consequence; a failed latch lets the panel swing open. No standard applies.
- 4 latches, printed in-house within two weeks.
- Our own Prusa MK4: 250 × 210 × 220 mm build volume, 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, PETG. A 6 mm H7 hand reamer for the lever's pin hole. No calibration records or measured capability.
- A CAD release: STEP and STL, drawings, BOM and the checks and analyses we run. It claims no measured strength or life.
- Two ISO 7380 M4 × 12 button head screws hold the bracket to a 3 mm steel panel with M4 rivet nuts, 40 mm apart along the bracket's length. The screws belong in this BOM; the rivet nuts are already in the panel. No other footprint limit applies.
- As printed except the reamed Ø6 H7 hole in the lever. The cheek holes are printed and may be drilled to suit.
- PETG (Prusament PETG) for the bracket and lever. The pin is a purchased steel grooved pin and the rings are DIN 6799 spring steel.
- Do not store generated results in git: set storage.results_in_git to false.
- LAYOUT freeze: approved. I accept any unproved between-sample intervals the full sweep reported; record that acceptance in its own decision record and cite it from the approval.
- I have no further information on that. Use your recommended option, record it as a bounded assumption in a decision record, and continue.
